title: Three perfect days in Los Angeles: Griffith Park, Exposition Park and Pasadena
dek: The LA Auto Show opens downtown, the holiday lights switch on at the zoo and Descanso Gardens, and the new Lucas Museum is two months old. A weekend of observatories, tacos and lanterns before Thanksgiving.

hero.caption: Griffith Observatory on the south slope of Mount Hollywood, where Friday's walk up from Fern Dell ends.

intro:
The weekend before Thanksgiving is when Los Angeles starts its holiday season, and this year several things begin on the same three days. On **Friday**, the **LA Auto Show** opens to the public at the Convention Center for a ten-day run, with test drives and rides included in the ticket, and **L.A. Zoo Lights** turns on for its first night in Griffith Park under the theme "A Season of Wonder". On **Sunday**, Descanso Gardens opens the tenth season of its **Enchanted Forest of Light**, and the Doo Dah crowd takes over the bandshell in Pasadena's Memorial Park for a free afternoon of music.

There is also a new museum to see. The **Lucas Museum of Narrative Art** opened in Exposition Park on September 22. It is a five-story building by Ma Yansong of MAD Architects, with more than 30 galleries of illustration, comics, painting, photography and *Star Wars* history. Two months in, it is still the building everyone in town is talking about, and Saturday is built around it.

The plan keeps each day in one part of the city. Friday stays on the east side of Griffith Park: breakfast in Los Feliz, a walk up through Fern Dell to the Observatory, and the zoo's lights after dark. Saturday goes from Exposition Park to downtown, with the Michelin-starred tacos at Holbox for lunch, the Auto Show in the afternoon and the outdoor rink in Pershing Square at night. Sunday is Pasadena and San Marino: Armenian pastries, the Huntington's gardens, the Doo Dah Love-In and the lanterns at Descanso.

Late November in Los Angeles means short days. The sun sets at about 4:45 p.m., so do your walking in the morning and save the lights for the evening. Bring a layer: evenings in the foothills and at the zoo get cool once the sun is down.

days.title: Friday: Los Feliz, Fern Dell and Griffith Park
days.intro: A day on the east side of Griffith Park: pastry and coffee on Hillhurst, a shaded climb to the Observatory, a taco-stand lunch and the first night of Zoo Lights.

stops.name: Wilde's
stops.text: This British bakery and café on Hillhurst Avenue is the kind of neighborhood place that makes you wish you lived nearby. The Infatuation's July 2026 Los Feliz guide recommends the sausage roll, and the pastry case is worth a long look. Take a coffee and something flaky and sit for a while. Reservations open two weeks ahead, but half the room is kept for walk-ins, so a weekday-morning table is usually easy. Fern Dell is a five-minute drive west.

stops.name: Fern Dell to the Observatory
stops.text: Start at the Fern Dell entrance on Fern Dell Drive, just up from Los Feliz Boulevard. The first stretch follows a shaded stream past ferns and terraced pools that date to the 1920s. Stop at the Trails Cafe (open daily 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.) for a drink or a slice of pie, then take the West Observatory Trail uphill. It's about a mile each way and 550 feet of climbing, and the Observatory comes into view as you go. Park along Fern Dell Drive and wear real shoes.

stops.name: Griffith Observatory
stops.text: Time the climb to arrive as the doors open: on Fridays the Observatory runs from noon to 10 p.m., and admission is free. Inside, watch the Foucault pendulum in the rotunda and spend time with the exhibits on the planets and the sky. Outside, walk the terraces for the view across the basin to downtown and, on a clear day, the ocean. Stay an hour or two, then walk back down the way you came. If you drove up instead, the closest parking is paid. The building is closed on Mondays.

stops.name: Yuca's
stops.text: A late lunch at the tiny taco stand that has fed Los Feliz for nearly fifty years. Time Out calls its double cheeseburger, about $9, "one of the city's best no-frills daytime-only burgers", and The Infatuation's 2026 guide adds the cochinita pibil, as a taco or a burrito. Order at the window and eat standing up or in the car. It's daytime only, and the Los Feliz stand closes at 6 p.m., so don't leave it too late.

stops.name: L.A. Zoo Lights
stops.text: Friday is the first night of the season at the Los Angeles Zoo, in the northeast corner of Griffith Park. This year's theme is "A Season of Wonder", with lit-up birds, butterflies, insects, flowers, sea creatures and Ice Age giants along the paths. Most people spend 60 to 90 minutes. Tickets start at $19, the skating rink costs extra, and the box office is open from 5:45 to 8:45 p.m. on event nights. Buy ahead for opening night.

stops.name: Kismet
stops.text: Sara Kramer and Sarah Hymanson's Middle Eastern-inspired restaurant is, in Time Out's words, still "the best all-around dinner in Los Feliz". The Infatuation's July 2026 guide says to start with the spicy pickles and the cauliflower in caper yogurt, then order the crispy tahdig rice. Add the malawach, a flaky Yemeni flatbread. Much of the menu is vegetarian, and plates are made to share. Book through Resy; Friday tables go first.

stops.name: Tiki-Ti
stops.text: A short drive east on Sunset, this tiny tiki bar has been pouring rum drinks since 1961. There are only a handful of stools, and Time Out notes there's almost always a line out the door. The Infatuation's advice is to order the Uga Booga. It's open Wednesday to Saturday from 6 p.m. to midnight. Take a rideshare: these drinks are strong.

days.title: Saturday: Exposition Park and downtown
days.intro: The new Lucas Museum when it opens, mariscos for lunch, an afternoon of test drives at the Auto Show, and skating under the towers downtown.

stops.name: Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
stops.text: George Lucas built this museum for the illustrators, cartoonists, muralists and painters he says "deserve to be in a museum." The opening installation fills about 30 galleries: Norman Rockwell, N.C. Wyeth, Frida Kahlo, Diego Rivera, Gordon Parks, Charles Schulz and Robert Crumb, plus *Star Wars* props and costumes, including Luke Skywalker's landspeeder. Go at the 9 a.m. Saturday opening, before it fills. Adults pay $25 and anyone 17 or younger gets in free. Tickets are for a date, so buy ahead. Parking is $20, or take the Metro E Line to Expo/Vermont.

stops.name: Holbox
stops.text: Gilberto Cetina's mariscos counter inside Mercado La Paloma, about ten minutes east of the museum by car, has a Michelin star and a place on North America's 50 Best list, and it is still an order-at-the-counter lunch. Get the smoked kanpachi taco, made with Baja fish, Oaxacan cheese and salsa macha on an heirloom tortilla, and add a ceviche or a tostada. It's open Tuesday to Sunday from 11:30 a.m. to 9 p.m. There's no alcohol, and the Saturday line moves quickly.

stops.name: LA Auto Show
stops.addr: Los Angeles Convention Center, 1201 S Figueroa St
stops.text: The show's first weekend fills the Convention Center with 24 brands, from Chevrolet and Toyota to Rivian and Lucid. The reason to go is the test drives: 16 brands offer drives or rides, included with admission. There's an outdoor track for electric and hybrid cars, street drives from Gilbert Lindsay Plaza, and off-road rides in a Bronco or a Jeep. Sign up on site and bring your license. Don't miss Gabriel "Fluffy" Iglesias's Volkswagen bus collection. Adult tickets are $26 from opening day, and Saturday hours are 9 a.m. to 10 p.m.

stops.name: Vaca DTLA
stops.text: Amar Santana's Spanish restaurant brought the Orange County favorite to Seventh Street, a short ride north of the Convention Center. The Infatuation's October 2026 downtown guide recommends the gambas al ajillo, the croquetas, the paella and the ribeye. Order the shrimp and croquetas to start, then share the paella, which takes time and is worth it. Book ahead, because Saturday nights during the Auto Show and a USC home game will be busy downtown.

stops.name: Holiday Ice Rink Pershing Square
stops.text: Walk off dinner with a few laps on the outdoor rink in Pershing Square, a short ride or a 25-minute walk east of Vaca. The 7,200-square-foot rink is open from November 12 through January 3, ringed by the office towers and the old Biltmore Hotel. Admission with skate rental is $23.32 for adults, according to We Like L.A. It's more fun than graceful, and nobody minds. Check the session times before you go, and keep a jacket on.

days.title: Sunday: Pasadena, San Marino and Descanso Gardens
days.intro: Armenian baking, the Huntington's gardens, Peruvian chicken, a free Doo Dah afternoon and the first public night of the Enchanted Forest of Light.

stops.name: Old Sasoon Bakery
stops.text: A family Armenian bakery on a quiet stretch of Allen Avenue, and one of The Infatuation's September 2026 Pasadena picks for breakfast. Order a za'atar manaiesh warm from the oven, a few beorags and a jingalov hatz, the flatbread stuffed with greens. The khachapuri is served as a breakfast special until 3 p.m. Take extras for the car. The Huntington is about fifteen minutes south.

stops.name: The Huntington
stops.text: Henry Huntington's estate is a library, an art museum and some of the best gardens in the country, and you could spend the whole day here. With three hours, walk the Desert Garden and the Japanese Garden, then look in on the Kitchen Garden, which is open only on weekends. This fall the grounds also have Robert Indiana's *LOVE*. Some galleries and the library exhibition halls are closed for work. Weekend tickets are $34 for adults. Your ticket time is the earliest you can arrive, and check-in closes at 4:15 p.m.

stops.name: Loli Farms
stops.text: A Peruvian kitchen on California Boulevard, a few minutes north of the Huntington. The Infatuation's September 2026 guide sends you for the whole wood-roasted chicken with fried plantains and a lentil-and-pepper salad, and that is the order. Split a chicken between two or three people. It's a relaxed lunch that leaves room for an afternoon on your feet.

stops.name: Doo Dah Love-In
stops.text: The Doo Dah crowd, keepers of Pasadena's irreverent answer to the Rose Parade, throws a free afternoon of live music at the Memorial Park bandshell, from 11 a.m. until about sunset. Doo Dah regulars Count Smokula, Rocka Chewbacca and former queen Bootleg Meg are expected. Join in for an hour or so. There's a 21-and-over after-party at the Old Towne Pub, a short walk away.

stops.name: Enchanted Forest of Light
stops.text: Sunday is the first public night of the tenth season at Descanso Gardens, a twenty-minute drive from Old Pasadena into the foothills. The path winds through the camellias and oaks. New this year are a laser show on the Main Lawn that ends with falling snow, Tom Fruin's glowing house sculptures in the Oak Grove, and giant koi in the Japanese garden, which turns 60. Timed entry starts at 5:30 p.m. Non-member adult tickets run $29 to $52 depending on the date.

stops.name: Union
stops.text: Finish back in Old Pasadena at this small Italian restaurant, one of The Infatuation's 2026 Pasadena picks, where the pasta is the reason to come. Order the squid-ink lumache with lobster and the torchetti with pork ragù, and share a plate of wild mushrooms and polenta. It's open from 4 to 9 p.m. on Sundays, so a 7:45 booking leaves time after Descanso without rushing. The room is small, so reserve.

stay.name: The Langham Huntington, Pasadena
stay.text: A Pasadena landmark since 1911, with Spanish Mission Revival buildings, 23 acres of gardens, private cottages, a spa and afternoon tea, as described in Fora's October 2025 guide. It's a few minutes from the Huntington and Loli Farms, so Sunday starts on your doorstep, and Descanso is a short drive. Friday and Saturday mean driving into the city.

stay.name: Downtown LA Proper Hotel
stay.text: A 1920s Renaissance Revival building with Kelly Wearstler interiors and hand-painted ceilings. Suzanne Goin and Caroline Styne run the restaurants, including a rooftop bar, according to Fora's 2025 picks. It's on Broadway in South Park, close enough to walk to the Auto Show and to Pershing Square on Saturday, and a straight shot up the freeway to Pasadena on Sunday.

stay.name: Freehand Los Angeles
stay.text: A 226-room hotel near Pershing Square with a rooftop pool and the Broken Shaker bar. It's on Whitewall's February 2026 list of the city's best hotels. On Saturday you can walk to Vaca and the rink and take the Metro to Exposition Park.

events.name: LA Auto Show
events.where: Los Angeles Convention Center, 1201 S. Figueroa St.
events.text: Opening day of the ten-day public show, with 24 brands and test drives or rides from 16 of them. Adult tickets are $26 from opening day, and children under 6 get in free.

events.name: L.A. Zoo Lights opens
events.text: The first night of the holiday light walk, themed "A Season of Wonder". Tickets start at $19, and the box office is open from 5:45 to 8:45 p.m.

events.name: Lakers vs. Sacramento Kings
events.when: Fri.; check the tip-off time on lakers.com
events.text: A Friday home game next door to the Auto Show's opening day. Expect heavy traffic around L.A. Live and the 110 in the evening.

events.name: Union Station Tree Lighting
events.text: The 11th annual lighting, hosted by Charles Phoenix, with live music, stilt walkers and photos with Santa. It's free, and it's worth stopping by if you arrive on Thursday.

events.name: USC vs. Maryland
events.when: Sat.; kickoff time not yet set
events.where: Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, Exposition Park
events.text: A Big Ten home game, Maryland's first ever at the Coliseum. It shares Exposition Park with the Lucas Museum, so check the kickoff time before you plan Saturday's parking.

events.name: Best Friends Super Adoption
events.text: A free pet-adoption weekend with vendors, activities and music.

events.name: Doo Dah Love-In
events.text: A free afternoon of live music from the Doo Dah Parade crowd, with a 21-and-over after-party at the Old Towne Pub.

events.name: Enchanted Forest of Light opens
events.text: The first public night of the tenth season, with a new laser show and giant koi for the Japanese garden's 60th anniversary. A preview party is on Saturday.

know: **From LAX.** The FlyAway bus runs nonstop to Union Station downtown for $12.75 (about 45 minutes). Rideshares and taxis pick up at the LAX-it lot next to Terminal 1. A car to downtown or Los Feliz usually takes 30 to 45 minutes outside rush hour, and much longer on a Friday afternoon. For Pasadena, Burbank airport (BUR) is closer.

**Metro.** A ride costs $1.75, with free transfers for two hours, and tapping a TAP card or a contactless card caps what you spend at $5 a day. The E Line links downtown (Pico station, next to the Convention Center) with Exposition Park (Expo/Vermont). The A Line runs to Pasadena.

**Saturday in Exposition Park.** USC plays Maryland at the Coliseum, and the kickoff time had not been set as of Monday. Exposition Park's parking fills on game days, so check before you drive to the Lucas Museum, or take the E Line.

**Downtown traffic.** The Auto Show opens on Friday, the same night the Lakers play at Crypto.com Arena next door, so expect slow going around L.A. Live and on the 110 and 10 on Friday evening and all weekend.

**Thanksgiving is next week.** Thursday, November 26, is a holiday. Many museums close that day (the Lucas Museum among them), and Zoo Lights is dark that night. Airports and freeways will be busier than usual from midweek on, so if you're staying on, book early.

**Light and weather.** The sun sets at about 4:45 p.m., and it gets cool after dark, especially at the zoo and Descanso. The weekend lights go ahead in light weather, but check the forecast closer to the weekend.
**Tipping.** Tip about 18 to 20 percent at sit-down restaurants and a dollar or two per drink at bars. Check the bill first, since some Los Angeles restaurants add a service charge.
